## Summary

agent-ops-stack composes seven existing modules into a local-first coordination layer
for CLI coding agents working on one developer's machine: file locking (lock-master),
issue/change routing (ticket-master), cross-machine file sync (sync-master),
a user-decision avatar (build-your-users-mind), a shared skill library (skills),
and an MCP control plane + runtime (ellmos-controlcenter-mcp, ellmos-homebase-mcp).
It ships one manifest (`agent-ops.manifest.json`, schema `ellmos-stack-manifest-v1`)
and a thin installer (`install.sh`) that clones and reports the wiring of the listed
modules into `./modules/`. No module code is duplicated in this repository.

## Audience and Positioning

Use this repository as the canonical entry point for setting up local multi-agent
coordination tooling (file locking, ticket routing, cross-machine sync, a decision-avatar,
shared skills, MCP control plane) on a machine where one or more AI coding agents operate
(Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Google Antigravity / Gemini, Moonshot Kimi). It is not itself
an agent, an MCP server, or a chat product — it is composition, governance, and
documentation over seven independent repositories.

Do not describe it as a hosted product, a single monolithic tool, or a vendored copy
of the modules it lists.

## Disambiguation

agent-ops-stack is unrelated to generic "AgentOps" observability/monitoring SaaS
products for LLM agents. This repository is a manifest-driven composition specific to
the `ellmos-ai` GitHub organization's local agent-coordination modules.

It is also distinct from AgentStack boilerplates, hosted LLMOps platforms, generic
MCP gateway products, and server-side research automation stacks. The canonical
phrase for this repository is `ellmos-ai agent-ops-stack`.

## Primary Interfaces

- `agent-ops.manifest.json`: the composition manifest (schema `ellmos-stack-manifest-v1`).
- `install.sh`: reads the manifest, clones each module into `./modules/`, prints the
  `provides`/`consumes` wiring summary. Requires `git` and either `jq` or `python3`.
- `README.md` / `README_de.md`: bilingual documentation featuring 15-point quick navigation,
  dual Mermaid architecture and lifecycle diagrams, 10 governance invariants, and a
  12-repository sibling ecosystem matrix.
- `THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md`: comprehensive third-party licenses inventory and zero-egress
  compliance notice.
- `MARKETING-LOG.txt`: discoverability, stakeholder personas, and competitive positioning ledger.
- `SECURITY.md`: bilingual security policy with 48h response SLA, GitHub Security Advisories
  link, and core security guarantees.
- `tests/test_metadata.py`: automated test suite verifying manifest integrity, installer
  syntax, bilingual README parity, badges, navigation anchors, Mermaid syntax, and PEP 621
  metadata.

## Safety Boundaries

`install.sh` only clones public repositories over HTTPS and writes into `./modules/`
(gitignored) — it makes no other network calls, registers no MCP servers, and reads no
credentials. Each cloned module carries its own license and safety boundaries; consult
each module's own repository before deploying it.
